description:
Moves the document methods off `CommandExecutor` onto the `documents()` facade, so a document consumer depends on `DocumentOps<'_, S>` instead of the whole executor surface.

## Background

`CommandExecutor` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs`) carries every command family in one public surface of about 195 methods across 28 `impl` blocks. The document family lives in `commands/document.rs` (`impl` at about :94): `add_document_reference`, `list_document_references`, `resolve_issue_artifact_directory`, `report_artifact_conformance`, `remove_document_reference`, `show_document_content`, `document_history`, `document_diff`, `read_document_content`, `read_document_bytes`, `get_document_history`, `get_document_diff`, `issue_documents`, `with_reported_documents`, `get_issue_document_paths`, `read_path_bytes`, `list_document_assets` and `check_document_links`. The HTTP server is this family's main consumer: `crates/server/src/routes.rs` calls `get_issue_document_paths`, `with_reported_documents`, `issue_documents`, `read_path_bytes`, `read_document_content`, `read_document_bytes`, `get_document_history` and `get_document_diff`. The CLI's `doc` arms in `crates/jit/src/main.rs` (or their handler module under `crates/jit/src/dispatch/`) and the document test suites are the other consumers.

The facade shape is fixed: `CommandExecutor::<family>()` returns a borrowing struct (`IssueOps<'_, S>` holds `&CommandExecutor<S>`), the family's methods live in `impl` blocks on that struct in the family's own `commands/` file, and each block keeps the storage bound its `impl CommandExecutor` block had (`IssueStore`, `IssueStore + RepositoryStateStore`, or concrete `JsonFileStorage`). The kernel (sessions, rule and config caches, `require_active_lease`, the validation `capture_*` helpers) stays on `CommandExecutor`; a facade method reaches it through its executor reference, and calls into another family go through that family's accessor.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `CommandExecutor::documents()` returns `DocumentOps<'_, S>`, and every public method listed in the Background is a method of `DocumentOps<'_, S>` rather than of `CommandExecutor`.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each `DocumentOps<'_, S>` impl block carries the same storage bound as the `CommandExecutor` block it replaces, so no method becomes callable on a storage it could not use before.
- [hard] REQ-03: Callers of the moved methods in `crates/jit`, `crates/server` and their test suites reach them through `documents()`, intra-doc links name the new paths, and the Rust workspace builds, lints and passes its existing suites with no assertion changed.

## Notes

- Behaviour, output and exit codes are unchanged; the compile plus the existing suites are the test boundary.
- Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md` (D-1, D-11); method inventory: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/investigation.md` area 3.
title: Document methods behind a documents facade
